findings.evidence: PROSE (disclosure of a behavioural consequence). Sandboxes = `git archive 2b7a820` and `git archive eefa94b`, each given the host's .claude/.qa-tracking/model-select-cache.json (`jq .timestamp` -> 2026-07-25T12:54:51Z; newest ids claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-5), run under `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY WORKFLOW_REVIEWER_LANE=codex WORKFLOW_DESIGN_REVIEWER_LANE=codex`, bd off PATH. (1) `model-select.sh apply --quiet --check` (the SessionStart call): base rc=0 `roles: ... (check-only: applied pins already match the config; 0 written)`; eefa94b rc=0 `resolver drift (config vs applied pins) - NOTHING auto-applied (R4-F1): designer: agent file has 'claude-fable-5-1', config resolves 'claude-fable-5' (apply: /workflow-model --role designer claude-fable-5); ...` for all five roles. (2) `statusline.sh` with envelope model.id=claude-opus-5-5: both trees render `des+dsr:fable-5 orch:opus-5 impl:sonnet-5 +1 more !sess`, which at eefa94b names ids no agent file pins (the render reads model-roles-resolved.json, which apply --check rewrites from the stale cache every session). (3) `model-select.sh check-parity`: base rc=0 OK; eefa94b rc=1 CONFIG/FILE DISAGREEMENT, fix text `/workflow-model --role <role> <old-id>, or model-select.sh apply`. (4) `workflow-doctor.sh --target <sandbox> --skip <all but model_parity>`: base rc=0 PASS model_parity; eefa94b rc=1 FAIL model_parity. COUNTERFACTUAL: the eefa94b sandbox with a cache that also lists claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 (two created_at orderings) -> apply --check `applied pins already match the config; 0 written`, check-parity rc=0. So the pins agree with .claude/model-roles and the disagreement is rk9y's stale listing alone. No automatic write path exists: session-start.sh:619-626 passes --check, and no installer or hook runs `model-select.sh apply` without it.
findings.description: Once this merges, any host whose model listing predates these models and has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (this host, per rk9y) gets three surfaces that present the OLD ids as the configured ones and print one-command reverts of this PR: the one line SessionStart shows, the statusline, and /workflow-doctor model_parity (so install.sh --verify too). The reverts are `/workflow-model --role <role> claude-*-5` and `model-select.sh apply`, which rewrites all nine pins and logs MODEL SWITCH comments to Beads. Nothing reverts by itself. The PR body discloses the disagreement in one general sentence. The shipped CHANGELOG entry does not mention it, nothing in the repo does, and .claude/commands/workflow-model.md:34-36 tells Claude to derive ids 'from ... SessionStart's model-select output'. A later session without the PR body in context therefore has every reason to 'fix' the drift. Fix, prose only: add to the CHANGELOG entry that until the listing is refreshed (rk9y) those three surfaces report drift and their suggested fixes are downgrades. Remedies verified in sandbox: an API-key refresh, or removing BOTH .claude/.qa-tracking/model-select-cache.json and model-roles-resolved.json. With both removed, SessionStart reads `no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set and no cached model list; keeping current pin`, the statusline reads `model: claude-opus-5-5`, and check-parity returns rc=2, so the doctor self-skips. Removing the cache alone leaves the statusline on the old ids.

findings.evidence: PROSE. `curl -sS https://formulae.brew.sh/api/cask/codex.json | jq .version` -> "0.160.0", so the cask installs the newest release. `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh` (fetched 2026-10-05) contains `RELEASE="${CODEX_RELEASE:-latest}"`, usage `install.sh [--release VERSION]`, and on a non-latest install `rm -f "$AUTO_UPDATE_VERSION"`, so a pinned install opts out of scheduled latest-channel updates. `install.ps1` declares `param([string]$Release = $env:CODEX_RELEASE)`, defaulting to latest.
findings.description: 'They install the newest release' is true of the Homebrew cask and of the two scripts' DEFAULT invocations, but both scripts accept an explicit release, so the sentence reads as if they cannot pin. The advice itself (pinned npm) is sound. npm is a hard dependency of the plugin (workflow-doctor's `deps` check). The registry's 0.145.0 package lists all six platform binaries as optionalDependencies (`curl -sS https://registry.npmjs.org/@openai%2fcodex | jq '.versions["0.145.0"].optionalDependencies'`). And npm is the only path verified for this lane. Suggested: 'They install the newest release by default. Both scripts accept a release (`--release 0.145.0`, `-Release 0.145.0`), but only the npm install was verified for this lane.'

findings.evidence: PROSE. The upstream release notes at github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.154.0 (fetched 2026-10-05) read: 'The deprecated `codex mcp-server` entry point is no longer available.' and '(#42993) Remove the deprecated `codex mcp-server` command'. They name no rename or new location. The scratchpad keeps no raw `codex --help` output for the eight probed versions: `find <S> -newermt '2026-10-05 06:00' -iname '*help*'` is empty, and mcp-probe.err holds only 'Error: stdin is not a terminal', with no version recorded.
findings.description: Line 9 still says `codex mcp-server` 'is documented upstream and is not labelled experimental'. Upstream deprecated it and then removed it in 0.154.0, so the page's header now contradicts the note directly below it. Separately, the new note's version boundary rests on --help probes whose output was not kept. The upstream release note independently confirms the 0.154.0 boundary and is worth citing. The registry confirms the rest: `latest` = 0.160.0, published 2026-10-01; 0.153.4 is followed directly by 0.154.0; and '0.155.x' is exactly 0.155.0 and 0.155.1, both probed. Info only.
